hero_eyebrow: A historic space with a modern spirit
hero_lede: A smaller guest list should not mean a smaller day. Everyone you actually want there, in a heritage building that already looks like the photographs, with the same all-inclusive package a hundred-guest wedding gets. If you have been hunting for a small wedding venue in Kitchener Waterloo and only finding halls built for two hundred, this is the other option.
objection_1_q: “Will a small wedding look lost in the space?”
objection_1_a: No, because you do not take the whole building. A micro wedding lives in the Library or the Lobby Bar, both sized for an intimate room, and the rest stays shut.
objection_2_q: “Do we still get the full package?”
objection_2_a: Yes. Same catering, same open bar, same AV, same onsite team. The package scales with the guest count, not the service level.
objection_3_q: “Is a venue worth it for forty people?”
objection_3_a: You are paying for a room that is already beautiful and a team that runs the night. That is worth more at forty guests than at a hundred, not less.
spaces_heading: Three Rooms That Suit A Short List
spaces_intro: You do not take the whole building. You take the room that fits.
space_1_body: Four 16-foot harvest tables and custom seating. One long table, one conversation, everyone in it.
space_2_body: Full bar and chandeliers. Right for a ceremony-and-cocktails evening with no seated dinner.
space_3_body: The colonnade and the two stone lions. The photographs happen here whatever the guest count.

microincl_heading: The Same Package, A Shorter List
microincl_intro: A micro wedding is not a stripped-back wedding. Everything below is in the quote at forty guests exactly as it is at a hundred.
why_1_body: An 1880 heritage building with original wood, ornate chandeliers, marble and coloured lighting. Couples arrive with flowers and a cake.
why_2_body: Venue, open bar, catering, AV, furniture, staff and parking quoted together. One team, one invoice, one point of contact.
